besluite.fout: The bare infinitive with an adverb wedged in ('help jou later onthou') reads loosely in written text.
besluite.rede: The full 'om ... te' form is clearer for a Grade 4 reader and the meaning is unchanged.

besluite.fout: The repeated 'en' in a three-part list reads wooden.
besluite.rede: A comma list is the natural written form, matches the heading, and keeps all three qualities.

besluite.fout: 'Laat staan' can be read as 'leave alone', so the sentence can mislead on a first reading.
besluite.rede: 'Opgestel' is the exact verb for setting a camera up on a tripod; the protected word 'driepoot' is untouched.

besluite.fout: 'Het lank gevat' is colloquial in written text.
besluite.rede: 'Lank nodig gehad' is standard written Afrikaans and says the same thing.
'Het lank geneem' for time is acceptable Afrikaans, and the proposal rebuilds the sentence around a protected wording without clear gain.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses with their own subject and verb ('druk jy' / 'die foto is').

besluite.rede: 'Sit' for an object's position is natural Afrikaans, and the shorter phrase could be read as working inside the camera.
'Al daardie tyd' is natural Afrikaans and points back to the wait; 'die hele tyd' is a lateral move that loses that link.
'Vir altyd' is natural and clear; 'vir goed' is itself close to an English calque and no better.

besluite.fout: The present tense 'hoef' jars in a paragraph told in the past, and the opening 'En' is weak written style.
besluite.rede: The proposal fixes tense and style; 'ook' carries the joining sense of 'En' without changing the meaning.

besluite.fout: The separable particle 'saam' sits mid-clause where standard written Afrikaans puts it at the end.
besluite.rede: Moving 'saam' to the end reads more naturally and changes nothing else.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses with their own subject and verb ('Oorloë is vasgelê' / 'die wêreld kon').

besluite.rede: The original split verb is normal Afrikaans word order, and 'bewaar' would repeat the verb of the list item just above it.
